hero.headline: Data Centers Ordered to Use Backup Power as Heat Wave Strains US Electric Grid
hero.body:
The Trump administration directed grid operators to require data centers to use backup power as triple-digit temperatures across much of the United States pushed the electric grid to its limits. The move aims to prevent blackouts as extreme heat drives up air conditioning demand while data centers consume massive amounts of electricity.

Grid managers issued emergency alerts as the heat wave stretched power systems to capacity. Data centers, which typically maintain backup generators for their own use during outages, were told to activate this reserve power to reduce strain on the main grid. The directive represents an unusual step to tap into privately held backup capacity during peak demand periods.

The power crisis highlights growing tensions between the rapid expansion of electricity-hungry data centers and grid reliability. Data centers have proliferated across the country to support cloud computing, artificial intelligence, and other digital services, but their power consumption has raised serious concerns about grid capacity and consumer costs.

Three Democratic senators have now launched an investigation into whether major tech companies are passing the soaring electricity costs of data centers on to ordinary Americans. Elizabeth Warren, Chris Van Hollen, and Richard Blumenthal sent letters to Google, Microsoft, Amazon, Meta, and several data center operators demanding greater transparency and accountability. In some regions with significant data center activity, residential electricity bills have increased by as much as 267 percent over the past five years, according to the lawmakers.

"Through these utility price increases, American families bankroll the electricity costs of trillion-dollar tech companies," the senators wrote. They are demanding that data centers and tech companies "pay their fair share of their electricity rates" and cover a greater share of costs upfront for future energy usage.

According to the US Department of Energy, data centers could account for 12 percent of the country's power consumption by 2028. About one-third of the nation's more than 4,000 data centers are located in just three states: Virginia, Texas, and California.

A Cornell study published recently in Nature Sustainability found that data centers could annually consume as much water as 6 million to 10 million Americans and emit as much carbon dioxide as 5 million to 10 million cars.

Opposition to data centers is growing across the country. Local efforts have blocked or delayed roughly 64 billion dollars in data center projects, according to a report published earlier this year by Data Center Watch. The lawmakers noted that contracts between data centers and utility companies are almost always confidential, leaving the public unaware of why their electricity bills continue rising.

One recent Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory study questioned the link between data centers and increasing electricity prices, finding that data centers may have actually helped reduce average retail electricity prices by allowing utility companies to spread fixed infrastructure costs among more power customers.

cards.headline: Russia Launches Deadly Strikes on Kyiv, Killing at Least 21
cards.body:
Russia deployed nearly 500 drones and more than 70 missiles in an hours-long assault on Kyiv and other parts of Ukraine in the early hours of Thursday, killing at least 21 people and injuring dozens more. City Mayor Vitali Klitschko described it as the worst Russian attack on the capital during more than four years of sustained air strikes against Ukraine.

Explosions rocked the city for several hours as waves of drones, cruise missiles, and ballistic missiles descended on multiple locations. Ukrainian air defense systems worked to intercept incoming weapons, but the sheer volume of the attack overwhelmed defenses across numerous areas. As dawn broke, fires burned at strike sites throughout Kyiv, with debris hitting residential buildings in several districts and a hotel on one of the central boulevards.

One of the most devastating impacts occurred on the left bank of the Dnipro River, where a large section of a nine-story apartment block was destroyed, reduced to rubble. Rescue teams spent the day searching through the remains hoping to find survivors. The death toll rose throughout Thursday and officials warned it could climb higher, with about 70 people hospitalized and rescue operations continuing.

President Volodymyr Zelenskyy had warned Ukrainians on Wednesday that a massive attack was likely. Speaking during a visit to Dublin, he urged people to use shelters and take precautions. In response, more than 50,000 residents took refuge in metro stations overnight, with some bringing mattresses and tents to sleep underground as the platforms became crowded.

Damage was recorded across 30 locations in the city, with most strikes hitting ordinary residential buildings. The Russian defense ministry claimed the attack targeted military facilities and energy infrastructure in retaliation for recent Ukrainian strikes, though it also hit regions outside the capital.

Upon returning to Kyiv, Zelenskyy visited one attack site and criticized international allies, saying that if they had provided air defense missiles as agreed, the damage would have been significantly less. "We are fighting alone. The victims are only Ukrainians," he stated.

The assault came as Ukraine has intensified long-range drone strikes against Russian oil refineries in recent weeks, causing fuel shortages across multiple Russian regions and prompting some areas to introduce petrol rationing. Ukrainian officials said they intended to maintain this pressure on Russian infrastructure.

Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha, visiting Japan, rejected claims that the strikes constituted legitimate retaliation. He stated that in the conflict between an aggressor and a defending nation, Ukraine has every right to strike military targets in Russia while Russia has no right to attack Ukrainian territory.

UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer called the attacks "a stark reminder that while Ukraine continues to pursue peace, Putin continues to inflict suffering and violence on the Ukrainian people."

cards.headline: Iran to Hold Funeral for Slain Supreme Leader Khamenei
cards.teaser: Long-delayed funeral ceremonies for Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, killed in strikes at the start of the Iran war, will begin Friday.
cards.body:
Funeral ceremonies for Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, killed during strikes by the United States and Israel at the outset of the Iran war, are scheduled to begin Friday. The ceremonies had been delayed for an extended period following his death.

For the Iranian regime, the funeral represents a significant moment to demonstrate continuity and resilience following the loss of its supreme leader. Officials view the event as an opportunity to show that the government has weathered the crisis and maintained control despite the leadership vacuum created by Khamenei's death.

cards.headline: U.S. and Iran Pause Talks for Khamenei Funeral After Claiming Progress
cards.teaser: Negotiations between the United States and Iran paused ahead of the slain ayatollah's funeral, with both sides reporting advances in discussions.
cards.body:
U.S. and Iranian negotiators held separate meetings in Qatar on Wednesday with mediators from Qatar and Pakistan. Both sides reported that positive progress had been made during the discussions.

The parties have agreed to resume talks following the funeral ceremonies for Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, whose funeral is scheduled to begin Friday.

cards.headline: Russian Strikes on Kyiv Deploy Record Number of Weapons
cards.teaser: The latest barrage on Ukraine's capital used more weapons than previous attacks and struck locations across a wide area.
cards.body:
Russian forces launched what Ukrainian authorities described as the most massive attack on Kyiv to date, deploying a record number of weapons in a coordinated strike. The barrage struck multiple locations across the capital, killing at least 21 people and destroying residential buildings, including a nine-storey apartment block that was completely destroyed.

The scale and distribution of the assault overwhelmed Ukrainian air defenses in several areas. The coordinated nature of the attack, spreading weapons across a wide geographical area of the city, made it difficult for defense systems to intercept all incoming drones and missiles.

cards.headline: Colorado wildfire becomes top national priority as fire doubles in size
cards.body:
The Aspen Acres Fire in Colorado has doubled in size and become the number one fire priority in the United States, prompting new evacuations and the closure of Highway 96. Fire officials warned that the blaze will continue to expand as extreme fire behavior is expected in the coming days.

The wildfire has forced additional residents to evacuate as it continues to spread through the region. Emergency crews are working to contain the fire, but conditions on the ground remain difficult. The closure of Highway 96 has disrupted travel in the area as authorities work to keep residents and motorists safe from the advancing flames.

Colorado has experienced challenging fire conditions this season, and the Aspen Acres Fire represents one of the most serious threats currently facing firefighting resources nationwide. The designation as the top national priority means the fire will receive first access to federal firefighting resources, including specialized crews and equipment from across the country.

Fire behavior analysts have indicated that weather conditions and terrain are creating circumstances for continued growth. The combination of dry fuels, wind patterns, and topography in the affected area has created a situation where rapid fire spread remains likely. Firefighters are working to establish containment lines, but officials have been clear that residents in surrounding areas should be prepared for potential evacuation orders.

The expansion of the fire has affected both residential areas and public lands. Authorities continue to monitor the situation closely and are coordinating with state and federal agencies to manage the response. Local officials have urged residents in nearby communities to stay informed about evacuation orders and to have plans in place to leave quickly if conditions worsen.

The wildfire emergency comes as multiple fires have erupted across western states this month, driven by dry, hot weather combined with high winds. The dangerous conditions have prompted governors in both Utah and Colorado to declare states of emergency. Utah's governor also issued a ban on personal fireworks until after the Fourth of July as a precaution against additional fire risks.

Thousands of firefighters have been deployed across western states and Alaska to combat the series of wildfires spreading rapidly through the region. The intensity of fire season has placed enormous strain on firefighting resources and personnel working in hazardous conditions.

State and federal agencies are coordinating response efforts, with the governor's office working alongside the Bureau of Land Management and other officials to contain the fires and protect communities in the path of the flames. Officials emphasized that residents should remain vigilant about evacuation notices and prepare to leave their homes on short notice if conditions deteriorate further.

cards.headline: Vatican Excommunicates Hundreds of Thousands in Breakaway Catholic Sect
cards.teaser: The Vatican excommunicated members of the Society of St. Pius X after the group consecrated bishops against the wishes of Pope Leo XIV.
cards.body:
The Vatican declared the Society of St. Pius X in schism after the traditionalist group consecrated bishops without papal approval. The action excommunicated the society's bishops, priests, and approximately 600,000 followers.

The conflict marks a major crisis for Pope Leo XIV. The Society of St. Pius X had previously maintained an ambiguous relationship with Rome, but its defiant decision to ordain bishops without the pope's consent triggered the formal break with the Catholic Church.

cards.headline: Germany Charges Ukrainian National in Nord Stream Pipeline Sabotage
cards.teaser: German prosecutors accused Kyiv of ordering the 2022 sabotage of the Nord Stream pipelines between Russia and Germany.
cards.body:
German prosecutors have charged a Ukrainian national in connection with the 2022 explosions that destroyed the Nord Stream pipelines carrying Russian gas to Europe. According to the indictment, the suspect, a former Ukrainian army officer, led the attack team and acted on orders from Ukrainian state authorities.

Ukraine has denied involvement in the case. The charges are expected to create significant tension between Kyiv and Berlin, which has been Ukraine's largest military supporter. The underwater sabotage in the Baltic Sea severely damaged the critical infrastructure linking Russia to European energy markets.

cards.headline: Venezuela Earthquake Survivor Rescued After Eight Days Trapped
cards.teaser: A man was pulled alive from beneath a collapsed multi-story car park more than a week after an earthquake struck La Guaira, Venezuela.
cards.body:
Hernán Gil was rescued alive after eight days trapped beneath a collapsed multi-storey car park in La Guaira, Venezuela, following an earthquake that struck the coastal region. Throughout the rescue effort, Gil remained in contact with workers, encouraging them as they carefully navigated through the rubble to reach him.

The rescue marked a hopeful moment in the aftermath of the devastating earthquake, which caused widespread destruction to buildings and infrastructure across the affected area.

cards.headline: Ryanair Warns of Airport Delays From New EU Border System
cards.teaser: The airline called on European governments to postpone the new Entry/Exit System until after the summer travel season.
cards.body:
Ryanair and other airlines are calling on European governments to suspend the new EU Entry/Exit System during peak summer travel season. The biometric border control system, designed to register non-EU travelers entering and exiting the Schengen Area, is already causing significant disruptions at airports across the continent.

Passengers are experiencing queues lasting up to five hours for biometric checks, and some flights are departing with empty seats as travelers avoid the system. Airlines and airports have urged European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen to allow the suspension of checks during the busy summer holiday period to prevent further travel chaos.

cards.headline: Paramedics responded to cardiac arrest call at Mitch McConnell's home before hospitalization
cards.teaser: Emergency medical services were called to the senator's residence for an unconscious patient on the day he was taken to the hospital.
cards.body:
Paramedics responded to a report of cardiac arrest at Senator Mitch McConnell's home on the same day he was hospitalized last month. Emergency medical service records indicate that responders were called for an unconscious patient at the residence.

The Kentucky senator was subsequently hospitalized following the incident. McConnell, who has served in the Senate for decades and previously held the position of Senate Majority Leader, has faced health concerns in recent years. The details of his current condition and treatment have not been fully disclosed by his office.

cards.headline: Supreme Court ruling affects Federal Trade Commission enforcement powers
cards.teaser: A recent Supreme Court decision has implications for how the FTC can exercise its regulatory authority.
cards.body:
The Supreme Court issued a decision that will affect the Federal Trade Commission's ability to enforce regulations and pursue enforcement actions. Legal analysts have been examining what the ruling means for the agency's future operations and its capacity to regulate business practices.

The decision comes amid broader debates about the scope of executive agency power and how federal regulators can implement their mandates. The ruling is expected to influence how the FTC approaches enforcement cases and regulatory actions going forward, potentially requiring the agency to adjust its strategies for protecting consumers and maintaining fair competition in the marketplace.

cards.headline: House Democrats allege Trump-backed Freedom 250 organization misled donors
cards.teaser: A report from Democratic lawmakers claims donors were deceived by the organization planning events for America's 250th anniversary.
cards.body:
House Democrats released a report accusing Freedom 250, a Trump-backed organization overseeing America's 250th anniversary celebration, of orchestrating corruption and fraud schemes. The investigation claims the group used a shadow corporation within the National Park Foundation to facilitate alleged pay-to-play schemes and wire fraud.

According to the congressional report, Trump staged a takeover of the milestone anniversary to enrich political allies, harvest voter data, and promote Christian nationalist ideology. Democrats say donors were deceived about how their contributions would be used.

cards.headline: Trump administration will not renew USMCA trade agreement
cards.teaser: The United States announced it will not extend the trade pact with Canada and Mexico, opening the door for new negotiations.
cards.body:
Updated Card

The Trump administration has refused to renew the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement, instead opting for annual reviews rather than committing to another 16-year term. The decision came Wednesday, the deadline for the three countries to jointly decide the pact's fate before its 2036 expiration.

By choosing short-term annual reviews, Trump is maintaining the trade framework while avoiding a long-term renewal of the deal he championed during his first term. This approach keeps the agreement in place but introduces ongoing uncertainty about its future, requiring the countries to reassess their commitment year by year.

cards.headline: Survivor rescued from rubble eight days after Venezuela earthquakes
cards.teaser: Hernan Gil was pulled alive from a collapsed parking structure more than a week after the disaster.
cards.body:
A survivor was rescued from the rubble of a collapsed multi-story car park in Venezuela eight days after earthquakes struck the region. Hernán Gil was trapped beneath the structure and encouraged rescue workers as they worked to reach him.

The rescue represents a rare success story in the aftermath of the earthquakes that caused widespread destruction across affected areas.

cards.headline: World Health Organization declares Hantavirus ship outbreak over
cards.teaser: No new cases have been reported since late May, according to the WHO director general.
cards.body:
The World Health Organization's director general has announced that a Hantavirus outbreak linked to a ship has ended, with no new cases reported since May 25.

Hantavirus typically spreads through contact with infected rodent droppings, urine, or saliva, and can cause severe respiratory illness in humans. The outbreak aboard the vessel prompted concerns about disease transmission in the confined maritime environment, but the WHO's declaration reflects the success of containment measures.

cards.headline: US Added Fewer Jobs in June as Unemployment Rate Ticked Down
cards.teaser: Employers added fewer jobs in June than the previous month, but the unemployment rate declined slightly in mixed economic signals.
cards.body:
US employers added just 57,000 new jobs in June, significantly below the roughly 120,000 economists had predicted. The Bureau of Labor Statistics also revised down figures from the previous two months by a combined 74,000 jobs.

Despite slower hiring, the unemployment rate dipped slightly to 4.2%. However, this decline was partly driven by 720,000 people leaving the labor force entirely, with the total number of unemployed people remaining essentially flat.

cards.headline: Dow Climbs Over 300 Points to Record High as Chipmakers Drag Down Nasdaq
cards.teaser: Stock markets moved in opposite directions Thursday as the Dow Jones Industrial Average hit a new record while technology stocks declined.
cards.body:
The Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed more than 300 points to reach a new record high Thursday, while the Nasdaq declined as semiconductor and chipmaker stocks faced selling pressure. The divergence reflected how investors were reassessing their positions across different sectors.

Chipmaker weakness was a key drag on the Nasdaq composite index. The contrasting movement between the major indices demonstrated investors rotating between sectors as they evaluated economic conditions and earnings outlooks.

cards.headline: Tesla Sales Jump 25 Percent in Europe After Price Cuts
cards.teaser: Tesla reported a strong recovery in European sales during the second quarter, driven by recent price reductions.
cards.body:
Tesla delivered over 480,000 electric vehicles globally in the second quarter, driven by geographic expansion and cheaper versions of its Model 3, Model Y, and Cybertruck. The surge marked a recovery for the automaker following a challenging sales year in 2025.

Europe emerged as a key growth region during the period, with price cuts playing a significant role in boosting demand. The European gains helped offset sales declines in the United States during the same quarter.

cards.headline: Blue Owl Reports Continued Investor Withdrawals from Private Credit Funds
cards.teaser: Investment firm Blue Owl disclosed another quarter of significant withdrawal requests from investors in some of its private credit funds.
cards.body:
Blue Owl reported significant investor withdrawal requests from some of its private credit funds in the latest quarter. The outflows continue a pattern of investor concern about the private credit sector.

The private credit industry has faced increased scrutiny over its rapid expansion and lending practices. Critics worry that firms in the sector extended loans to companies that may lack the ability to repay them, raising questions about the stability of these investments.

cards.headline: Goldman Sachs to Deposit $1,000 into Trump Accounts for Eligible Employee Children
cards.teaser: Goldman Sachs announced it will contribute $1,000 to Trump Accounts for eligible children of its employees.
cards.body:
Goldman Sachs said it will make $1,000 contributions to Trump Accounts for eligible children of its employees. The announcement comes as the Trump Account program prepares to launch on July 4, offering government-backed savings accounts for newborns.

The Trump Account program gives newborns $1,000 in seed money from the government. Goldman Sachs joins other employers offering additional contributions to the accounts for their workers' children. Treasury officials have said the investment options will include exchange-traded funds from State Street, BlackRock, and Vanguard.

cards.headline: Ryanair Warns New EU Border System Will Cause Airport Delays
cards.teaser: The airline called on European governments to postpone the Entry/Exit System until after summer travel season.
cards.body:
Ryanair and other airlines have warned that the EU's new Entry/Exit System for biometric border checks is causing severe disruptions at airports. Passengers are experiencing queues lasting up to five hours, and some flights are departing with half-empty seats as travelers miss their departures.

Airlines and airports have urged European leaders to suspend the system during the peak summer holiday season. In a letter to European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, the industry called for the option to temporarily halt the biometric checks, citing concerns that congestion will worsen significantly as travel demand increases.

hero.headline: US government intelligence network hacked, senator warns of national security risk
hero.body:
A cybersecurity breach has compromised an intelligence-sharing network operated by the Department of Homeland Security, prompting a senior Democrat on the Senate Intelligence Committee to raise alarms about potential national security consequences.

The hacked system allows various government agencies to share sensitive intelligence with one another. The senator's warning indicates that accessed information could include details about security operations, though authorities have not publicly detailed what was actually taken during the intrusion.

This represents another significant cybersecurity incident affecting US government infrastructure. Federal agencies have repeatedly struggled to defend their networks from intrusions. Previous breaches have exposed employee records, internal communications, and classified materials across multiple departments.

The Department of Homeland Security has not yet publicly announced when the breach took place or identified which threat actors may have been responsible. As the agency that coordinates domestic security efforts and partners with state and local law enforcement agencies, its networks represent a valuable target for foreign intelligence services seeking to gather information about American security operations and vulnerabilities.

The timing of this incident reflects broader concerns about government cybersecurity practices. A series of high-profile breaches across federal agencies has prompted increased Congressional attention to network defense standards and incident response procedures. Members of Congress have called for stronger protective measures and faster detection and notification capabilities when breaches occur.

However, implementation of these security improvements has proceeded unevenly across different departments. Some agencies have made significant investments in upgraded defenses and monitoring systems, while others have moved more slowly in modernizing their cybersecurity infrastructure. Budget constraints and the complexity of protecting legacy systems have contributed to these disparities.

Intelligence-sharing platforms present particularly significant security challenges because they consolidate information from multiple agencies into centralized systems. This aggregation makes them high-value targets for attackers seeking to access classified or sensitive information that might otherwise be scattered across separate networks with different security protocols.

The breach underscores ongoing vulnerabilities in how the federal government protects critical systems. With foreign adversaries and criminal organizations continuing to develop sophisticated attack capabilities, federal cybersecurity officials face persistent pressure to stay ahead of emerging threats.

As this latest incident demonstrates, even systems handling some of the government's most sensitive information remain vulnerable to compromise. The incident will likely intensify debates within Congress about whether current funding levels, technical standards, and agency accountability measures are adequate to protect national security information.

The full scope of the breach and its potential consequences may not become public for some time, as investigations proceed into what occurred and how the intrusion was ultimately discovered.

cards.headline: OpenAI proposes giving US government 5 percent equity stake
cards.teaser: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has offered to give the US government a 5 percent ownership stake in the company.
cards.body:
Sam Altman is in early-stage talks with the Trump administration about giving 5 percent of OpenAI's equity to a proposed US sovereign wealth fund. Altman has argued that this approach would allow the American public to share in the financial benefits generated by artificial intelligence development.

The proposal would reportedly involve other AI companies making similar contributions. This revives broader discussions about structuring public participation in the economic gains from the AI industry's rapid growth.

cards.headline: Tesla reports 25 percent sales increase in second quarter
cards.teaser: Tesla's vehicle deliveries rose 25 percent in the second quarter of 2026 compared to the same period last year.
cards.body:
Tesla delivered more than 480,000 electric vehicles globally in the second quarter, marking a significant recovery for the automaker. The company produced 451,758 vehicles during the period, with the majority being Model 3 and Model Y vehicles.

Deliveries exceeded production, indicating Tesla has reduced its inventory levels after facing stockpiles of unsold vehicles in previous quarters. The sales surge appears driven by geographic expansion and the availability of more affordable versions across Tesla's lineup.

cards.headline: Advocacy groups urge FTC to reject ending oversight of X
cards.teaser: Privacy advocates are asking federal regulators to maintain monitoring of Elon Musk's X platform.
cards.body:
Consumer advocacy groups have asked the Federal Trade Commission to reject Elon Musk's request to end regulatory oversight of X, formerly Twitter. The advocates cite concerns about user privacy and the platform's artificial intelligence initiatives as reasons for continued monitoring.

Musk has sought to terminate a consent decree that subjects X to FTC monitoring following past privacy violations. The advocacy groups argue that ending oversight would pose serious risks to Americans' personal data, particularly as the company expands its AI capabilities and data usage.

cards.headline: TV Time app shutting down as parent company shifts to AI products
cards.teaser: The TV-tracking app TV Time will shut down on July 15 as its parent company pivots toward enterprise AI.
cards.body:
Whip Media is shutting down TV Time, its popular app for tracking television shows and movies, on July 15. The company is pivoting toward developing artificial intelligence products for enterprise clients in the entertainment industry.

The shutdown will leave TV Time's consumer audience without the service, as Whip Media has not announced any plans to transfer user data or provide an alternative platform.

cards.headline: Lucid Motors CFO departs as new CEO reshapes leadership
cards.teaser: Lucid Motors' chief financial officer has left the company as part of an executive restructuring.
cards.body:
Lucid Motors' CFO has departed as the company's new CEO continues restructuring the executive team. The automaker has announced several new executive appointments as part of efforts to improve performance and turnaround.

The leadership changes come as the Gravity SUV has underperformed sales expectations. The moves appear aimed at addressing challenges facing the electric vehicle manufacturer in a competitive market.

cards.headline: Launch problem delays NASA satellite rescue mission
cards.teaser: A last-minute technical issue has postponed a planned satellite rescue mission for NASA.
cards.body:
NASA has delayed a satellite rescue mission due to a launch problem that emerged shortly before the scheduled liftoff. The mission aims to service or retrieve a satellite currently in orbit.

The space agency has not announced a new launch date. Technical issues during the final countdown are common in spaceflight operations and often require teams to recycle launch preparations. NASA typically provides updates on rescheduled launch windows after engineers resolve identified problems.

hero.headline: Celtics trade Jaylen Brown to 76ers for Paul George in blockbuster deal
hero.body:
The Boston Celtics have agreed to send Jaylen Brown to the Philadelphia 76ers in exchange for Paul George, two first-round draft picks, and two second-round selections, according to ESPN's Shams Charania. The deal represents a significant reshaping of both Eastern Conference rosters as the franchises pursue championship aspirations.

Brown, the 2024 NBA Finals MVP, departs Boston after developing into one of the league's premier stars. His move to Philadelphia comes after what reports describe as a stormy few weeks, during which Brown expressed unhappiness with his treatment by the Celtics organization. The 76ers are acquiring a player at the peak of his powers to pair alongside Joel Embiid as they attempt to maximize their championship window.

The Celtics will receive draft compensation that provides flexibility for future roster construction. The first-round picks are scheduled for 2028 and 2031, while the two second-round selections offer additional asset value. Boston will retain Jayson Tatum as their franchise centerpiece while adding George, a veteran forward with championship experience and a reputation for strong two-way play.

For the 76ers, Brown represents the offensive firepower needed to complement Embiid. The pairing gives Philadelphia two All-Star caliber players capable of leading a deep playoff run. The trade signals that the 76ers view this as their opportunity to compete at the highest level, even if it means sacrificing future draft assets.

George brings defensive versatility and proven scoring ability to the Celtics, giving Boston a veteran presence to anchor their continued contention efforts. His addition maintains Boston's status as a perennial Eastern Conference threat despite losing Brown.

This trade is the latest in a series of significant offseason moves across the NBA, as franchises attempt to construct rosters capable of winning a title. Both organizations have made calculated decisions about their rosters and timelines. The Celtics have essentially traded a younger star for veteran complementary pieces and future flexibility, while the 76ers have committed their resources to winning now around Embiid.

The deal remains pending standard league approval and medical examinations for both players involved. Once finalized, it will reshape the competitive landscape of the Atlantic Division and provide both teams with new identity entering the upcoming season.

The trade deadline for both organizations has now passed, and both will turn their focus to developing chemistry among their new roster configurations. How these rosters perform on the court will determine whether each franchise's approach to the trade deadline proves successful.

cards.headline: Belgium rallies from two goals down to beat Senegal 3-2 in World Cup extra time
cards.teaser: Youri Tielemans converted a penalty in stoppage time of extra time to complete Belgium's comeback from a two-goal deficit.
cards.body:
Belgium defeated Senegal 3-2 in the World Cup round of 32 on Wednesday, completing a remarkable comeback from two goals down. Youri Tielemans sealed the victory with a penalty kick in stoppage time of extra time, sending Belgium through to the next round.

Senegal built an early commanding lead, but Belgium mounted a determined rally during regulation to level the match and force the extra period. Tielemans' late penalty proved decisive in one of the tournament's most dramatic turnarounds.

cards.headline: United States beats Bosnia-Herzegovina 2-0 for first World Cup knockout win since 2002
cards.teaser: The USMNT secured its first World Cup knockout round victory in 24 years with a 2-0 win over Bosnia-Herzegovina.
cards.body:
The United States men's national team defeated Bosnia-Herzegovina 2-0 in the World Cup round of 32 on Wednesday night. The victory marks their first knockout stage win at the World Cup since 2002, ending a 24-year drought in elimination matches.

The win advances the USMNT to the next round of the tournament.

cards.headline: Rays third baseman Junior Caminero homers in sixth consecutive game
cards.teaser: Junior Caminero has become the youngest player since at least 1900 to homer in six straight games.
cards.body:
Tampa Bay Rays third baseman Junior Caminero hit a home run in his sixth consecutive game, joining an exclusive group in baseball history. At just 22 years old, Caminero became the youngest player since at least 1900 to accomplish the feat.

The achievement represents a remarkable power display during a stretch that has helped bolster the Rays' offensive production as the team progresses through the regular season.

cards.headline: Alex Ovechkin to return for 22nd season with Washington Capitals
cards.teaser: The NHL's career goals leader will play another season with the team where he has spent his entire professional career.
cards.body:
Alex Ovechkin will return to the Washington Capitals for the 2026-27 season, extending his career to 22 seasons. Ovechkin holds the NHL record for career goals and has played his entire professional career with the Capitals franchise.

The decision means Ovechkin will continue pursuing additional records and milestones. His return provides the Capitals with their longtime captain and leading scorer as they prepare for the upcoming season.

cards.headline: Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift to marry at Madison Square Garden
cards.teaser: The wedding is scheduled for Friday night at the New York venue, according to a law enforcement official familiar with security arrangements.

cards.headline: Pirates ace Paul Skenes allows season-high seven runs in loss to Phillies
cards.teaser: Skenes lasted only four innings and gave up seven earned runs in a 10-6 defeat.
cards.body:
Pittsburgh Pirates pitcher Paul Skenes struggled against the Philadelphia Phillies, allowing seven earned runs over four innings in a 10-6 loss. The seven earned runs represented a season high for Skenes, who has been one of the team's top starters.

Skenes acknowledged his poor execution after the game. The abbreviated outing marked an uncharacteristic performance for the ace, whose season statistics took a significant hit in the defeat.

hero.headline: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce to Wed Friday at Madison Square Garden
hero.body:
Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce announced their engagement on Tuesday after a two-year relationship, with the couple sharing the news on Instagram. The 35-year-old singer posted a joint message with the Kansas City Chiefs tight end that read: "Your English teacher and your gym teacher are getting married" alongside photos of Kelce on one knee in a floral setting.

According to People magazine, Kelce proposed with a ring designed by New York City-based jeweler Kindred Lubeck of Artifex Fine Jewelry. The announcement generated immediate fan excitement, with Google displaying celebratory confetti when users searched Swift's name.

Law enforcement officials have confirmed that the couple plans to celebrate their wedding at Madison Square Garden on Friday night, according to security briefings obtained by multiple outlets. The NYPD memo details arrangements for the event, including dress code requirements and guest policies. The Associated Press obtained a permit showing the wedding schedule for the Manhattan venue.

Swift and Kelce have been together since July 2023, when their relationship began during Swift's Eras Tour. Kelce initially attempted to give Swift his phone number on a friendship bracelet at a Kansas City concert stop. When that failed, he publicly discussed his interest in the singer on his podcast, New Heights. He told his brother Jason Kelce that he was disappointed Swift did not interact with fans before or after shows because she needed to preserve her voice.

The couple officially launched their relationship publicly in September 2023 when Swift attended an NFL game at Arrowhead Stadium to watch Kelce play for the Chiefs. Since then, they have made frequent headlines together. Following the Chiefs' Super Bowl LVIII victory in 2024, Swift and Kelce were photographed kissing on the field in front of thousands of fans.

Swift has incorporated Kelce into her performances, including modifying the song "Karma" during Eras Tour shows to reference him. She also featured him during a London performance in 2024. Recently, both appeared on New Heights to announce Swift's upcoming 12th album, The Life of a Showgirl, which many suspected would precede an engagement announcement. That podcast episode broke YouTube records for concurrent views, drawing 1.3 million simultaneous viewers when it first aired on August 13, with the episode accumulating 20 million total views by Tuesday.

Ahead of the wedding, Swift and Kelce announced they donated $26 million to at least 20 charities this week. The couple has not publicly confirmed their wedding plans beyond the law enforcement documentation.

The NFL congratulated the couple on their engagement. Brittany Mahomes publicly expressed support, calling them "two of the most genuine people." Donald Trump also offered well wishes, describing Kelce as "a great player" and Swift as "a terrific person."

cards.headline: Madonna Releases Confessions II Album
cards.teaser: The pop singer has released a new album that critics are calling her strongest work in two decades.
cards.body:
Madonna released Confessions II, a dance-focused album that marks her return to old-school dance music 21 years after the original Confessions on a Dance Floor. The album was inspired by her 2023 Celebration tour, which led her to reflect on her past work and incorporate references throughout the record.

The album features a house-influenced sequence of tracks that flow together like a DJ mix, similar to the original 1989 album's structure. It also draws from the trip-hop sound of Madonna's Bedtime Stories, concluding with slower, more introspective material. The Guardian described it as her most vital album in two decades, noting vivid vignettes of 1980s New York life.

cards.headline: LaRoyce Hawkins to Leave Chicago PD During Season 14
cards.teaser: The actor who has played Officer Kevin Atwater since the NBC drama launched will exit the series.
cards.body:
LaRoyce Hawkins will leave Chicago PD during the show's upcoming 14th season, according to sources who confirmed the news to Variety. Hawkins has appeared in the NBC police drama since its premiere, playing Officer Kevin Atwater.

The method of the character's departure is not being disclosed. Chicago PD is one of the longest-running series in NBC's primetime lineup and part of producer Dick Wolf's Chicago franchise, which includes Chicago Fire and Chicago Med.

cards.headline: Gary Glitter Charged With Additional Sexual Abuse Offenses
cards.teaser: The Rock N Roll Part 2 singer faces new charges while serving a 16-year sentence for crimes against schoolgirls.
cards.body:
Gary Glitter, the British glam rock musician whose real name is Paul Gadd, has been charged with historical sexual offences. He is scheduled to appear at Westminster Magistrates' Court on August 5.

Gadd, who found fame in the 1970s with his hit "Rock N Roll Part 2," is currently serving a 16-year prison sentence for previous convictions related to sexual abuse against schoolgirls. He was sentenced in 2015 for those historical offenses.

cards.headline: Lisa Faulkner Says She Is Cancer-Free After Treatment
cards.teaser: The British actress and presenter said she had surgery and is feeling much better following a breast cancer diagnosis.
cards.body:
Lisa Faulkner announced she is all clear after being diagnosed with breast cancer. The actress, presenter, and food writer disclosed that she underwent what she described as a big operation.

Faulkner said she is feeling so much better following the surgery and treatment. She is known for her work in British television as both an actress and a food presenter.

cards.headline: Married at First Sight UK Cast Member Arrested on Rape Allegation
cards.teaser: A star of the Channel 4 reality series was arrested following a BBC investigation into the show.
cards.body:
A cast member from the Channel 4 reality show Married at First Sight UK has been arrested on suspicion of rape, following a BBC Panorama investigation that aired in May.

The dating series pairs strangers together to marry for the first time, with relationship experts overseeing the matches. It has become a ratings success for the network.

cards.headline: Crunchyroll Founder Launches Anime Licensing Platform AniBiz
cards.teaser: Kun Gao's new company has created the first business-to-business marketplace built specifically for the anime industry.
cards.body:
Nakama, a media company founded by former Crunchyroll CEO Kun Gao, launched AniBiz.com on Thursday. The platform is described as the first dedicated business-to-business marketplace for the global anime industry, featuring offerings from major rights holders including Aniplex and Toei.

Gao leads the venture alongside co-founders Brady McCollum, who serves as CEO, and Sae Whan Song. The platform is designed to facilitate licensing deals and business transactions in the anime sector, which has grown significantly in international markets over the past decade.

hero.headline: Federal appeals court blocks firing of intelligence officers assigned to diversity roles
hero.body:
A federal appeals court has upheld a lower court decision preventing the Trump administration from firing 19 career intelligence officers who worked on diversity, equity, inclusion and accessibility programs. The 4th Circuit Court of Appeals issued a 2-1 ruling Thursday, finding that the administration violated federal employment protections when it terminated these officers.

The intelligence officers held career positions within federal agencies and were assigned to roles focused on diversity and inclusion work when they were dismissed. They challenged their terminations in court, prompting the initial lower court to block the firings. The Trump administration subsequently appealed that decision to the 4th Circuit.

Career federal employees receive protections under civil service regulations that restrict how easily they can be removed from their positions. These protections differ significantly from those covering political appointees. The appeals court's decision suggests the administration did not follow proper procedures when it terminated these officers based on their work assignments in diversity-related roles.

The ruling represents a legal obstacle to the administration's broader effort to eliminate diversity positions across federal government agencies. One judge dissented from the majority opinion in the case, though specific details about the dissent were not disclosed in available reports.

The 4th Circuit Court of Appeals has jurisdiction over federal cases from Maryland, Virginia, West Virginia, North Carolina and South Carolina. This geographic area includes federal agencies headquartered in the Washington region, making the circuit court a significant venue for cases involving national security and intelligence agencies.

With this ruling in place, the 19 intelligence officers will retain their positions while the legal process continues. The Trump administration retains the option to pursue further appeals, potentially requesting a review by the full 4th Circuit panel or petitioning the United States Supreme Court for consideration. No announcement regarding next steps came immediately after the decision was issued.

The case highlights ongoing tensions between the Trump administration's push to curtail diversity initiatives within government and the legal protections afforded to career federal employees. Federal employment law requires that terminations follow established procedures and cannot be undertaken solely based on an employee's job assignment or role, particularly when that employee holds permanent civil service status.

The decision may have broader implications for other federal agencies facing similar efforts to eliminate diversity positions. Other branches of government employing career staff under civil service protections could face comparable legal challenges if they attempt similar terminations without adhering to required procedures.

cards.headline: Trump administration issues emergency orders to boost electrical output ahead of heat wave
cards.teaser: The White House issued emergency orders Wednesday to maximize electrical output as an extreme heat wave threatens power shortages during Fourth of July weekend.
cards.body:
The Trump administration issued emergency orders Wednesday to maximize electrical output as an extreme heat wave threatens the country ahead of the Fourth of July weekend. A heat dome is expected to blanket the East Coast and extend across the South through Saturday's celebrations marking America's 250th anniversary.

The dangerous temperatures have raised concerns about strain on the electrical grid as millions of Americans use air conditioning during the holiday weekend. Safety worries are growing over the numerous planned celebrations across the country as the extreme heat persists.

cards.headline: Trump financial disclosure shows $2 billion income, crypto venture brought in $526 million
cards.teaser: President Trump's financial disclosures showed he brought in $2 billion last year, with his crypto venture managed by the Trump Organization generating over $526 million.
cards.body:
President Trump's financial disclosures reveal he earned over $2 billion last year, with cryptocurrency ventures accounting for more than $1 billion of that income. His crypto operations significantly outpaced earnings from real estate and Trump-branded merchandise like watches.

The Wall Street Journal's editorial board criticized Trump and his family this week, arguing they are "cashing in on the presidency in big and sketchy ways." The disclosures raise concerns about potential conflicts of interest, particularly given Trump's efforts to deregulate the crypto industry from which he profits substantially.

cards.headline: Some Trump administration figures suggest limiting pregnant women from entering US after citizenship ruling
cards.teaser: Members of the Trump administration have suggested limiting entry of pregnant women into the country following the Supreme Court's ruling upholding birthright citizenship.
cards.body:
I don't have a source that directly covers the story about Trump administration figures suggesting limits on pregnant women entering the US after the citizenship ruling. The additional source material provided covers different topics (USMCA trade deal, US anniversary celebration, and OpenAI).

Since the source material is about a different story, I'm returning the original card text unchanged:

Members of President Trump's administration have suggested the United States should limit the entry of pregnant women into the country following a Supreme Court decision on birthright citizenship. The high court ruled 6-3 on Tuesday to strike down a Day 1 executive order from Trump that sought to limit birthright citizenship only to children of citizens and legal permanent residents.

The Supreme Court decision upheld the constitutional guarantee of citizenship for anyone born on US soil. The suggestions to restrict pregnant women from entering the country have come from far-right figures, including some within the Trump administration, in response to the ruling.

cards.headline: Republican senator says Trump's voting legislation is dead ahead of midterms
cards.teaser: Sen. Thom Tillis said the SAVE America Act lacks time for implementation before November elections, even if it gained the necessary Senate votes.
cards.body:
Sen. Thom Tillis of North Carolina declared the SAVE America Act, President Trump's top legislative priority, dead on Capitol Hill. He cited insufficient time to implement new election laws before November's midterm elections as the reason.

Tillis noted that even if Senate Republicans secured the 60 votes required to advance the legislation—which he views as unlikely—the timeline would not permit changing voting rules before the elections. The assessment signals a significant setback for the White House's legislative agenda.

cards.headline: Chuck Todd says Trump's midterm convention will benefit Democrats
cards.teaser: The former Meet the Press host said President Trump's upcoming midterm convention will help Democrats by nationalizing the races.
cards.body:
Former Meet the Press host Chuck Todd said Wednesday that President Trump's upcoming midterm convention will help Democrats heading into the November elections. Todd said Democrats would likely welcome the event because it nationalizes the midterm races.

Todd suggested that Democrats might even help pay for the convention, noting that nationalized midterm elections typically favor the party out of power. The more national attention focused on the races, Todd said, the better the outcomes tend to be for the opposition party in midterm election cycles.

cards.headline: Northern lights could be visible over July 4 weekend
cards.teaser: Nature may provide its own colorful nighttime display over the Independence Day weekend as northern lights could be visible in some areas.
cards.body:
The northern lights could illuminate the sky during the July 4 weekend, potentially offering a natural light show to complement fireworks and other Independence Day celebrations. The aurora borealis typically appears only at far northern latitudes but can occasionally be seen further south when solar activity increases.

The timing could make for a memorable holiday weekend as Americans gather for celebrations across the country. Skywatchers in areas with heightened solar activity may have a chance to witness the colorful natural phenomenon alongside traditional holiday festivities.
